name: South Dakota

agency.name: South Dakota Department of Labor and Regulation, Division of Labor and Management

rates2026.note: Indexed annually to CPI, rounded up to the nearest 5 cents

tipped.note: Half the minimum wage; employer must ensure tips bring pay to $11.85. Tipped = more than $35/month (dol.gov table).

source.quote: The minimum wage for non-tipped employees in South Dakota is $11.85/hour . (Effective Jan. 1, 2026.)

overtime.note: No state overtime law; federal FLSA applies.

source.quote: South Dakota has no labor laws concerning compensatory (comp) time or overtime.

sickLeave.note: No statewide paid sick leave law for private employers.

finalPay.fired: by the next regular payday (or when the employee returns employer property, if later)
finalPay.quit: by the next regular payday (or when the employee returns employer property, if later)

source.quote: Whether an employee quits or is fired, the law requires that all wages and compensation be paid not later than the next regular stated pay day
South Dakota does not have a law requiring an employer to provide rest breaks and meal periods.

rightToWorkSource.quote: The right of any person to work may not be denied or abridged on account of membership or nonmembership in any labor union or labor organization.

notes.text: South Dakota's minimum wage is adjusted every year to the cost of living and can never decrease; the increase is rounded up to the nearest 5 cents.

source.quote: The amount of the increase will be rounded up to the nearest 5 cents. The minimum wage cannot decrease.

notes.text: Tipped workers' cash wage is half the minimum ($5.925 in 2026), higher than the federal $2.13.

source.quote: The minimum wage for tipped employees in South Dakota is $5.925 /hour . (Effective Jan. 1, 2026.)

uncertain: 2027 rate not yet announced on dlr.sd.gov as of 2026-10-11 (usually announced in the autumn).
